facts.fact: At the July 2026 allmyt Summit Mauritius Telecom's CEO Veemal Gungadin said H200 GPUs were already available in the company's data centre in Mauritius, as reported by devfactory.mu.

devfactory.mu observed on 8 August 2026 that Mauritius Telecom's public myt AI Cloud catalogue lists seven models, including its own myt_asr speech-to-text and myt_tts text-to-speech services, with H200 compute in Mauritius behind the platform.

systems.platform: multi-model AI API with OpenAI-compatible endpoint

MUS.note: The Mauritius Telecom data centre is named only as hosting H200 GPUs; the document does not say it rents space or computing to others.
No rule that data must be kept in the country is stated.
Only a company's sovereignty framing and an unproven residency claim; nothing on state data rules, hosting or contract terms.
No statement that a data centre for hire is nationally owned or Tier rated.
Mentions startups only as potential customers; no startup law, labelling or fund.
No hub, incubator or park is described.
